claims.text: The surface area of a square pyramid is the area of the base plus the area of the triangular sides.
For a square pyramid, surface area = b² + 4(½ b h_s), where b² is the area of the base and each of the 4 triangular sides has area ½ b h_s.
The surface area of a square pyramid simplifies to b(b + 2h_s).
The surface area of a triangular pyramid is the area of the base plus the area of the triangular sides.
For a triangular pyramid, surface area = (½ b × h_b) + 3(½ b × h_s), where (½ b × h_b) is the area of the triangular base and 3(½ b × h_s) is the area of the three triangular sides.
The surface area of a triangular pyramid simplifies to ½ b (h_b + 3h_s).
To find the surface area of a triangular pyramid, first find the area of the base triangle using area = ½ b h_b.
The height of the base triangle (h_b) is found using the theorem of Pythagoras.

claims.text: The area of the sector is ½ × base × height (of a small triangle).
Taking the base as 2πr and the height as a, the area of the sector is ½ × 2πr × a = πra.

The area of the circular base is A_b = πr².
The area of the curved walls is A_w = πra = πr√(r² + h²).
The surface area A of the cone is the sum of the areas, A = A_b + A_w = πr² + πr√(r² + h²).

items.stem: If a cone has a height of $h$ and a base of radius $r$ , show that the surface area is: $\pi{r}^{2}+\pi r\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{h}^{2}}$
solution: Sketch and label the cone: [figure]

Identify the faces that make up the cone: The cone has two faces: the base and the walls. The base is a circle of radius $r$ and the walls can be opened out to a sector of a circle: [figure] This curved surface can be cut into many thin triangles with height close to $a$ (where $a$ is the slant height). The area of these triangles or sectors can be summed as follows: $\begin{align*}\text{Area of sector}&=\frac{1}{2}\times\text{base}\times\text{height (of a small triangle)}\\&=\frac{1}{2}\times2\pi r\times a\\&=\pi ra\end{align*}$
Calculate $a$: $a$ can be calculated using the theorem of Pythagoras: $a=\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{h}^{2}}$
Calculate the area of the circular base ( ${A}_{b}$ ): ${A}_{b}=\pi{r}^{2}$
Calculate the area of the curved walls ( ${A}_{w}$ ): $\begin{align*}{A}_{w}&=\pira\\&=\pir\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{h}^{2}}\end{align*}$
Find the sum of the areas $A$: $\begin{align*}A&={A}_{b}+{A}_{w}\\&=\pi{r}^{2}+\pir\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{h}^{2}}\\&=\pir\left(r+\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{h}^{2}}\right)\end{align*}$
